findings.body: MessageBuilder raises a missing interpolation argument while generating the email, so that email is not delivered.
findings.evidence: To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).
findings.failure_mode: Unrelated email paths fail during template rendering after opting into the existing unsubscribe behavior.
findings.impact: MessageBuilder raises a missing interpolation argument while generating the email, so that email is not delivered.
findings.root_cause: The shared unsubscribe translation was changed to unconditionally interpolate a value that only topic notification emails provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the generic `unsubscribe_link` translation free of topic-only placeholders and add the topic link through a notification-specific translation or only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.
findings.title: Global unsubscribe translation requires an argument unavailable to other mailers
findings.trigger: A mailer such as the rejection mailer opts into `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying a topic-specific `unsubscribe_url`.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch changes `unsubscribe_link` to unconditionally interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. MessageBuilder.body (line 90) calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. Callers like rejection_mailer set `add_unsubscribe_link` without providing `unsubscribe_url`, causing I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument.

findings.body: The next access to `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError`, and the unsubscribe page returns an error instead of changing the preference.
findings.failure_mode: A valid unsubscribe request cannot complete for users lacking per-topic state.
findings.impact: The next access to `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError`, and the unsubscribe page returns an error instead of changing the preference.
findings.root_cause: The new action assumes that every notification recipient already has a TopicUser row.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `TopicUser.change` with the desired notification level, or create a TopicUser row when the lookup returns nil before reading its level.
findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.trigger: An authenticated user follows the link for a notification received from a topic where no `topic_users` row was previously created, such as a mention without a prior topic visit.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 105 uses `find_by` which returns nil when no TopicUser exists. Line 107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without nil check, causing NoMethodError for users who received notifications without visiting the topic.

findings.body: The current template must preserve the typo and correctly named consumers fail to find the property, reducing discoverability and making refactoring error-prone.
findings.failure_mode: Naming-based lookup and maintenance produce avoidable missing-property errors.
findings.impact: The current template must preserve the typo and correctly named consumers fail to find the property, reducing discoverability and making refactoring error-prone.
findings.root_cause: The new public controller property was introduced with `Notificiations` misspelled.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the property to `stopNotificationsText` and update the unsubscribe template reference.
findings.title: The unsubscribe controller property is misspelled
findings.trigger: A future template or controller lookup uses the correctly spelled `stopNotificationsText`, or a maintainer searches for the notification text property.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows `stopNotificiationsText` with 'Notificiations' misspelled (extra 'i'). The template at unsubscribe.hbs line 3 uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` matching the typo, so it works but creates maintenance burden.

raw_findings.body: Ruby attempts to compare nil with an integer and raises `ArgumentError`, so the email link fails.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing TopicUser records with no explicit notification level cause a server error on unsubscribe.
raw_findings.impact: Ruby attempts to compare nil with an integer and raises `ArgumentError`, so the email link fails.
raw_findings.root_cause: The action compares the nullable database value directly instead of applying the model's regular-level default.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize a NULL level to the regular default before comparison, or delegate the transition to `TopicUser.change` and its default handling.
raw_findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes for TopicUser rows with a null notification level
raw_findings.trigger: The user has a TopicUser row created without `notification_level`, leaving the column NULL, which is supported elsewhere by the model's COALESCE logic.

raw_findings.body: The existing auto-tracking logic can promote the muted/regular row back to tracking because the unsubscribe was not marked as a user change, causing topic notifications to resume.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A user preference change is later indistinguishable from an automatically managed preference and can be overwritten.
raw_findings.impact: The existing auto-tracking logic can promote the muted/regular row back to tracking because the unsubscribe was not marked as a user change, causing topic notifications to resume.
raw_findings.root_cause: The action bypasses TopicUser's change API and persists only `notification_level`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the level through `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which records `notifications_changed_at` and the user-changed reason.
raw_findings.title: Direct save leaves auto-tracking metadata unchanged
raw_findings.trigger: A user unsubscribes from a row whose `notifications_reason_id` is NULL, then later reads the topic long enough to satisfy the automatic tracking threshold.

raw_findings.body: The other view keeps displaying the old notification state and its controls remain stale until a later reload.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Clients observing the topic do not receive the state transition performed by the new endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: The other view keeps displaying the old notification state and its controls remain stale until a later reload.
raw_findings.root_cause: The action uses ActiveRecord save directly and skips TopicUser's notification-change publication.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `TopicUser.change`, or explicitly publish the notification-level change through the same MessageBus path used by other notification updates.
raw_findings.title: Unsubscribe changes are not broadcast to other open topic views
raw_findings.trigger: The user has the same topic open in another browser tab or window subscribed to the topic MessageBus channel when the unsubscribe request completes.

raw_findings.body: The user's per-topic notification preference changes without an intentional interactive action, and a tracking/watch level may only be reduced to regular on the first request rather than being fully unsubscribed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Transport-layer URL fetching is treated as user intent and can produce unexpected or incomplete unsubscribe results.
raw_findings.impact: The user's per-topic notification preference changes without an intentional interactive action, and a tracking/watch level may only be reduced to regular on the first request rather than being fully unsubscribed.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new GET action performs a stateful notification-level transition as soon as the URL is fetched.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the operation idempotent and use a signed, one-time confirmation flow or a CSRF-protected state-changing request instead of mutating preferences directly on GET.
raw_findings.title: The state-changing unsubscribe endpoint is vulnerable to unintended GET execution
raw_findings.trigger: A logged-in user's mail client, link previewer, browser prefetcher, or an unrelated page causes a GET request to the unsubscribe URL; repeated requests can also apply different transitions.

raw_findings.body: The localized email still contains only the account-level preferences link, so the per-topic unsubscribe feature is unavailable and the UI behavior differs by locale.
raw_findings.evidence: To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Localized output silently loses the feature while English output exposes it.
raw_findings.impact: The localized email still contains only the account-level preferences link, so the per-topic unsubscribe feature is unavailable and the UI behavior differs by locale.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the English shared translation was updated even though the same key is defined in other locale files.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the topic-specific link to every supported translation or introduce a separate notification-specific key with an intentional fallback strategy.
raw_findings.title: Non-English notification emails omit the new per-topic unsubscribe option
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose site locale has an existing translated `unsubscribe_link` string, such as German or French, receives a topic notification email.

validated_findings.impact: The localized email still contains only the account-level preferences link, so the per-topic unsubscribe feature is unavailable and the UI behavior differs by locale.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only the English shared translation was updated even though the same key is defined in other locale files.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add the topic-specific link to every supported translation or introduce a separate notification-specific key with an intentional fallback strategy.
validated_findings.title: Non-English notification emails omit the new per-topic unsubscribe option
validated_findings.trigger: A user whose site locale has an existing translated `unsubscribe_link` string, such as German or French, receives a topic notification email.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a documentation/localization gap rather than a bug introduced by the patch. The patch only modifies server.en.yml. Missing translations in other locales is a pre-existing pattern, not a defect introduced by this change.

validated_findings.body: The test can still pass because the assertion checks `builder`, not `message_with_unsubscribe`, and therefore does not validate the new URL behavior.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A regression in per-topic unsubscribe rendering is not detected by the advertised coverage.
validated_findings.impact: The test can still pass because the assertion checks `builder`, not `message_with_unsubscribe`, and therefore does not validate the new URL behavior.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new fixture argument was added without changing the existing assertions to inspect that fixture.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Assert the body and HTML of `message_with_unsubscribe`, including the expected `/t/1234/unsubscribe` URL and its rendered link.
validated_findings.title: The new unsubscribe URL fixture is not asserted by the message-builder spec
validated_findings.trigger: The test suite runs while the unsubscribe URL interpolation or rendered link is accidentally removed or broken.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds `unsubscribe_url` to the fixture at line 172 but existing assertions at lines 175 and 179 check `message_with_unsubscribe.header_args` and `builder.template_args[:user_preferences_url]` respectively - neither validates the new unsubscribe_url is rendered correctly.

validated_findings.body: The current template must preserve the typo and correctly named consumers fail to find the property, reducing discoverability and making refactoring error-prone.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Naming-based lookup and maintenance produce avoidable missing-property errors.
validated_findings.impact: The current template must preserve the typo and correctly named consumers fail to find the property, reducing discoverability and making refactoring error-prone.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new public controller property was introduced with `Notificiations` misspelled.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the property to `stopNotificationsText` and update the unsubscribe template reference.
validated_findings.title: The unsubscribe controller property is misspelled
validated_findings.trigger: A future template or controller lookup uses the correctly spelled `stopNotificationsText`, or a maintainer searches for the notification text property.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 5 shows `stopNotificiationsText` with 'Notificiations' misspelled (extra 'i'). The template at unsubscribe.hbs line 3 uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` matching the typo, so it works but creates maintenance burden.
